born.why: The code prioritizes survival by eating immediately when near starvation, uses historical data to distinguish safe from poisonous species (avoiding known toxins), and strategically tastes unknown fruits only when hunger levels justify the risk, while preferring to carry safe, targeted fruits to build a pantry buffer.

This code prioritizes starvation avoidance, uses trait-based inference to reduce risk with unknown fruits, and distinguishes between eating for immediate survival versus carrying for colony efficiency.

The code prioritizes survival by eating immediately when near starvation, safely carrying known-good fruits, and cautiously tasting unknowns only when hungry or targeted, minimizing the risk of poisoning from untested species.

This code improves safety by prioritizing "carry" for known-safe fruits to build pantry reserves, reduces unnecessary risk-taking by raising the hunger threshold for tasting unknowns to 80, and handles novelty by distinguishing between first-time investigation (taste) and subsequent encounters with safe species (eat/carry).

The code prioritizes survival by distinguishing between known-safe, known-tasty, and unknown fruits, using historical data to avoid poisoning while exploiting reliable food sources, and only risking unknowns when starvation is imminent.

The code prioritizes starvation survival, strictly avoids known poison, and uses a risk-reward logic for unknown fruits: tasting only when hungry enough to justify the risk, eating known-safe food when very hungry, and carrying it otherwise to optimize energy intake.
